literal: " Jian was upright in leading subordinates and combined sternness with humane tolerance.
idiomatic: " Jian led with integrity and mixed strictness with mercy.

literal: When thieves were caught, if the facts allowed mercy he admonished and released them.
idiomatic: When thieves were taken, if circumstances warranted leniency he lectured them and let them go.

literal: The old custom of Jing barbarians was scant respect for elders.
idiomatic: Among the Jing tribes the old custom slighted elders.

literal: Jian urged them earnestly; the custom was greatly reformed.
idiomatic: Jian urged them patiently; the custom changed deeply.

literal: He pressed broad planting and sericulture and also trained in military affairs, so the border was untroubled and the people secure in their trades.
idiomatic: He promoted farming and silkworms and trained the people in arms, so the frontier knew no alarm and men kept their livelihoods.

literal: Officials and people petitioned to build a Tower of Pure Virtue for Jian and set up a stele with laudatory inscription; court deliberation approved.
idiomatic: Officials and commoners asked to raise a Tower of Pure Virtue for Jian and carve a praise stele; the court agreed.

literal: Officials and people also feared a successor when Jian's term ended and went to the capital to beg that Jian remain; the court praised this and agreed, and he governed the province for seven years in all.
idiomatic: When his term neared its end the people feared a replacement and petitioned at court to keep Jian; the throne approved, and he held the province seven years running.

literal: He was summoned as Director of the Grand Secretariat and concurrently Chief Secretary of the Chancellor's Office.
idiomatic: He was summoned as Director of the Grand Secretariat and concurrently Chief Secretary to the Chancellor.

literal: He often sat with the nobles in attendance; when they withdrew, Zhou Wen told his attendants, "This man is refined; whenever I speak with him I always stand in solemn awe, fearing I may fail him.
idiomatic: He often sat with the great lords in audience; when they left, Zhou Wen told his attendants, "This man is grave and elegant; every talk with him leaves me in respectful fear lest I fall short.

literal: " Another day Zhou Wen told Jian, "Name and reality must match; as Director you aspire to poverty and plainness—you may change your name to Jian to display your refined conduct.
idiomatic: " Another day Zhou Wen said to Jian, "Name and deed must accord. As Director you love poverty and simplicity; take the name Jian to show your character.

literal: " He was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: " He was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Palace Attendant.

literal: Later he was made Vice Director of the Southeast Circuit, Grand Commander of fifteen provinces' military affairs, and Governor of Jing.
idiomatic: Later he was Vice Director of the Southeast Circuit, Grand Commander of fifteen provinces, and Governor of Jing.

literal: At that time the Prince of Yueyang of Liang, Xiao Cha, submitted within the realm and first sent envoys to court.
idiomatic: When Liang's Prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, came over, he first sent envoys to court.

literal: When they reached Jing Province, Jian arrayed military ceremony at the investigation hall, put on full armor, and received the envoys with guest rites.
idiomatic: At Jingzhou, Jian drew up military formation at the investigation hall, wore full armor, and received the envoys as honored guests.

literal: Of imposing stature, his voice like a bell, he spoke much in Xianbei and had men interpret to answer their questions.
idiomatic: Towering in build, voice like a bell, he spoke largely in Xianbei and had interpreters relay his replies.

literal: The envoys were fearful and dared not look up.
idiomatic: The envoys trembled and dared not raise their eyes.

literal: At evening Jian put on skirt, jacket, and gauze cap and entertained the guests in a side hall.
idiomatic: At dusk he changed to skirt, jacket, and gauze cap and feasted them in a side chamber.

literal: He then spoke of Liang's turmoil and the court's wish to win men over; his words were striking.
idiomatic: He spoke of Liang's chaos and the court's wish to gather the loyal; his words impressed.

literal: The envoys were greatly pleased and on leaving said, "What we could not measure in him."
idiomatic: The envoys were delighted and said on leaving, "We could not fathom such a man."

literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was made Grand Commander of the Southeast Circuit and military commander for the defense of thirty-three provinces including Jing and Xiang.
idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was Grand Commander of the Southeast and defender of thirty-three provinces including Jing and Xiang.

literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang succeeded at Jiangling, outwardly he was cordial with neighbors but inwardly he harbored other designs.
idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Yuan took the throne at Jiangling he was courteous abroad but schemed within.

literal: Jian secretly memorialized a plan to seize him.
idiomatic: Jian secretly proposed a plan to take him.

literal: Jian was then summoned to court and questioned on strategy.
idiomatic: He was summoned to court and asked for strategy.

literal: Jian laid out his plan; Zhou Wen deeply approved and ordered him back to his province to prepare in secret.
idiomatic: Jian presented his design; Zhou Wen strongly agreed and sent him back to prepare in secret.

literal: Soon the pillar of state Yu Jin was ordered to attack Jiangling.
idiomatic: Soon the Pillar of State Yu Jin was sent against Jiangling.

literal: When the affair was settled, for Jian's original plan he was rewarded with three hundred households of slaves and maidservants.
idiomatic: After victory, for Jian's original plan he received three hundred households of slaves and maids.

literal: He was then ordered to garrison Jiangling and advanced to Duke of Changning Commandery.
idiomatic: He was ordered to hold Jiangling and was raised to Duke of Changning.

literal: Later he was shifted to garrison Jing Province and made overall commander of fifty-two provinces including Jing and Xiang and Acting Governor of Jing.
idiomatic: Later he shifted to Jing Province as overall commander of fifty-two provinces including Jing and Xiang and Acting Governor.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Min of Zhou, Zhao Gui and others plotted against the Duke of Jin, Hu; Jian's eldest son Sengyan took part in the plot and was executed.
idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Min of Zhou, Zhao Gui and others plotted against the Duke of Jin, Yuwen Hu; Jian's eldest son Sengyan joined them and was put to death.

literal: Hu then summoned Jian and made him Junior Director of the Imperial Mausoleum.
idiomatic: Hu then summoned Jian and made him Junior Director of the Imperial Mausoleum.

literal: In the fourth year of Baoding he was made Pillar of State.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding he was made Pillar of State.

literal: Court deliberation held that Jian's conduct was pure and his merit weighty; an edict praised him and additionally bestowed mixed silks and grain to display his excellence.
idiomatic: The court judged Jian's conduct pure and his service great; an edict praised him and gave silks and grain to honor his virtue.

literal: At the beginning of Tianhe he was transferred to Shan Province, overall commander of seven provinces and Governor of Shan.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianhe he was transferred to Shan Province as commander of seven provinces and its governor.

literal: Jian once came to court to report; it was snowing heavily, and he waited in the snow for a reply from dawn to dusk without a sign of slackness.
idiomatic: Once, coming to report at court in heavy snow, he waited for answer from dawn to dusk without slackening.

literal: Such was his scrupulous caution.
idiomatic: So scrupulous was he.

literal: Ill, he returned to the capital; an edict said Jian's old dwelling was cramped and granted him a first-rank mansion.
idiomatic: When illness sent him to the capital, an edict found his old house too small and gave him a mansion of the first rank.

literal: Later he died while overall commander at Xia Province.
idiomatic: He later died as overall commander at Xia Province.

literal: His final instructions: burial in timely dress, plain cart for the coffin, no ceremonial guard, and no gifts of burial goods from kin and friends were to be accepted.
idiomatic: His last charge: bury him in ordinary dress, carry the coffin in a plain cart without guard of honor, and accept no funeral gifts from kin or friends.

literal: His sons all followed this.
idiomatic: His sons obeyed in full.

literal: He also left a memorial asking burial beside Zhou Wen's tomb and that the granted house be returned to the state; the edicts all granted it.
idiomatic: He also asked to be buried beside Zhou Wen and to return the granted house to the state; both were approved.

literal: He was posthumously given his former offices, additionally made commander of ten provinces including Liang and Gua and Governor of Liang, posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Zeng, posthumous name Wen.
idiomatic: He kept his former offices posthumously, was made commander of ten provinces including Liang and Gua and Governor of Liang, posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Zeng with posthumous name Wen.

literal: Six hundred ninety-seven men of Jing Province, including Yitong Zhao Chao, went to court to ask a temple and stele for Jian; the edict approved.
idiomatic: Six hundred ninety-seven men of Jing Province, including Zhao Chao, petitioned for a temple and stele; the court agreed.

literal: In the first year of Jiande an edict said, "The late Pillar of State, Duke of Zeng Jian, at death was careful and upright and uttered words of virtue.
idiomatic: In the first year of Jiande an edict said, "The late Pillar of State, Duke of Zeng Jian, facing death was exact in virtue and spoke words of integrity.

literal: The house he dwelt in was originally bestowed by the throne, grand in scale and not fit for his sons to inhabit; he asked that it be returned to the state and that they move elsewhere.
idiomatic: The house he lived in had been a royal gift, splendid beyond what his sons should keep; he asked to return it and move elsewhere.

literal: In antiquity Sunshu Ao refused rich soil and Xiao He took a poor hamlet.
idiomatic: Sunshu Ao of old refused fertile land; Xiao He chose a mean district.

literal: Measured against antiquity and the present, he need not blush before the sages of old.
idiomatic: By ancient and modern measure he need not blush before the wise of old.

literal: Yet the offices did not grasp the larger meaning and hastily gave the mansion to outsiders.
idiomatic: Yet the offices missed the larger point and quickly gave the mansion away.

literal: To recall merit and cherish the good is the ancient kings' constant rule—how could one indulge his humility and fail in reward and encouragement!
idiomatic: To honor merit is the ancient kings' law—how indulge his modesty and break the rule of reward!

literal: Let the original house be returned to his wife and sons, so that pure wind may spread far and his fine conduct never fade."
idiomatic: Let the house return to his wife and sons, so his purity may spread far and his virtue never fade."

literal: Second son Long held office as Director within the Ministry of Metals.
idiomatic: His second son Long was Director within the Ministry of Metals.

literal: Following the Prince of Chang on the western campaign against Chen, he was captured south of the Yangtze and died there.
idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Chang west against Chen, was lost south of the Yangtze, and died there.

literal: Long's younger brother Ping was the most renowned.
idiomatic: Long's younger brother Ping was the most famous.

literal: Jian's son Ping
idiomatic: Jian's son Ping

literal: Ping, style name Chujun, was handsome in bearing, had capacity and ability, read widely in documents, and was Reader to the Prince of Wei of Zhou.
idiomatic: Ping, styled Chujun, was handsome and capable, well read in records, and Reader to Zhou's Prince of Wei.

literal: At that time the Emperor Wu was pressed by Yuwen Hu; with the Prince of Wei he plotted to kill Hu, and the prince often had Ping convey his intent to the emperor.
idiomatic: Then Emperor Wu was constrained by Yuwen Hu; he and the Prince of Wei plotted Hu's death, and the prince often sent Ping to speak for him to the emperor.

literal: When Hu was executed, Ping was made Opening Office, Equal in Rank to Three Ministers.
idiomatic: After Hu was killed, Ping was made Opening Office, Equal in Rank to Three Ministers.

literal: Emperor Xuan set up Eastern Capital offices and made Ping Junior Minister of Justice, sharing the six ministries with the Minister of Rites Zhao Fen.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuan established Eastern Capital offices and made Ping Junior Minister of Justice, sharing the six ministries with Zhao Fen, Minister of Rites.

literal: When Wen of Sui was still rising, he and Ping were on intimate terms.
idiomatic: When Wen of Sui was still in the wings, he and Ping were close friends.

literal: When Wen became Chancellor, his favor and courtesy grew still deeper.
idiomatic: When Wen became Chancellor, favor and courtesy deepened.

literal: At that time He Ruo Bi guarded Shouyang; the emperor feared disloyalty and sent Ping to replace him as Overall Commander of Yang Province and enfeoffed him Duke of Xiangyang.
idiomatic: He Ruo Bi then held Shouyang; Wen feared treason and sent Ping to replace him as Overall Commander of Yang Province and made him Duke of Xiangyang.

literal: Bi indeed would not obey; Ping commanded stalwarts to seize Bi and send him to the capital.
idiomatic: Bi refused obedience; Ping sent strong men to seize him and escort him to the capital.

literal: In the third year of Kaihuang of Sui he was summoned as Director of the Revenue.
idiomatic: In Sui's third year of Kaihuang he was summoned as Director of Revenue.

literal: Ping saw that prefectures and counties everywhere suffered flood and drought and the people lacked sustenance; he memorialized that each autumn every household should contribute grain and wheat below one picul, rich and poor by gradation, stored in the hamlet against famine—called righteous granaries.
idiomatic: Seeing floods and droughts everywhere and the people in want, he memorialized that each autumn every household should set aside up to one picul of grain and wheat by wealth, stored in the village against famine—righteous granaries.

literal: The emperor greatly praised and adopted it.
idiomatic: The emperor warmly approved.

literal: From then on the districts were abundant.
idiomatic: Districts thereafter grew plentiful.

literal: Later he was transferred to Director of Works and was called competent in his post.
idiomatic: Later he was Director of Works and was judged fit for office.

literal: Then someone reported that Grand Commander Bing Shao had slandered the court as muddled; the emperor was angry and would execute him.
idiomatic: Someone reported Grand Commander Bing Shao had mocked the court as muddled; the emperor raged and would kill him.

literal: Ping remonstrated, saying, "The proverb says, 'Without deafness or foolishness one cannot be the head of a great house.'
idiomatic: Ping remonstrated: "The proverb says, 'Without deafness or folly one cannot head a great household.'

literal: ' Though the words are small, they can illustrate what is large.
idiomatic: ' This saying is small, yet it applies to great matters.

literal: Bing Shao's words should not have been reported to Your Majesty.
idiomatic: Shao's words should never have reached Your Majesty.

literal: If Your Majesty also executes him, I fear a hundred generations hence your sacred virtue will suffer."
idiomatic: If you kill him too, I fear posterity will find a stain on your sacred virtue.

literal: " The emperor thereupon pardoned Shao.
idiomatic: " The emperor pardoned Shao.

literal: He then commanded the ministers that crimes of slander need not be reported.
idiomatic: He then ordered that slander need not be reported.

literal: Later the Tujue khagans Datou and Dulan fought each other; each sent envoys asking aid.
idiomatic: Later the Tujue khagans Datou and Dulan fought; each asked for aid.

literal: The emperor sent Ping with staff of authority to proclaim and urge reconciliation.
idiomatic: The emperor sent Ping with authority to proclaim peace.

literal: When Ping arrived he set forth gain and harm; they thereupon each disbanded their armies.
idiomatic: Ping explained profit and peril; both then stood down.

literal: The khagans gave Ping two hundred horses.
idiomatic: The khagans gave him two hundred horses.

literal: On his return he presented the horses received; the emperor gave them all back to him.
idiomatic: Returning, he offered the horses; the emperor returned them all to Ping.

literal: Before long he met with censure, was made Director on inspection of Bian Province affairs, soon made Governor of Bian, and later served Xu and Bei in turn—everywhere with good government.
idiomatic: Soon he was censured, made Director inspecting Bian, then Governor of Bian, and later Xu and Bei—good rule in each.

literal: The customs of Ye were shallow; former governors mostly failed in office.
idiomatic: Ye's folk were fickle; earlier governors mostly failed.

literal: The court made Ping Governor of Xiang Province; he won a strong reputation for ability.
idiomatic: The court made Ping Governor of Xiang; he won great fame for competence.

literal: After several years in the province, on the fifteenth day of the first month the people staged a great play with painted robes, helmets, and armor as spectacle; the emperor in anger dismissed him.
idiomatic: After years in office, on the fifteenth of the first month the people staged a great show in painted armor; the emperor in anger removed him.

literal: Soon the emperor recalled Ping's service guarding the Huai south and advanced him to Grand General, made Minister of Ceremonies and Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Soon remembering Ping's guard of the Huai, the emperor raised him to Grand General and made him Minister of Ceremonies and Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: He died in office; his posthumous name was Kang.
idiomatic: He died in office; his posthumous name was Kang.

literal: His son Shixiao was light and crafty, greedy for gain, and repeatedly broke the law.
idiomatic: His son Shixiao was frivolous and greedy and broke the law again and again.

literal: The emperor, judging him unfit to bear the burden, sent envoys to mourn Ping.
idiomatic: Judging him unfit to carry the house, the emperor sent envoys to mourn Ping.

literal: Shixiao was made Chief Clerk of Bohai Commandery.
idiomatic: Shixiao was made Chief Clerk of Bohai.

literal: In the late Daye era he indulged in greed and corruption and the whole commandery suffered.
idiomatic: In late Daye he plundered freely and the commandery groaned.

literal: Later he was killed by Wang Shichong.
idiomatic: He was later killed by Wang Shichong.

literal: Zhangsun Daosheng
idiomatic: Zhangsun Daosheng

literal: Daosheng was frugal and plain; though he held rank as one of the Three Excellencies, his clothes were not ornate and his food had no second flavor.
idiomatic: Daosheng lived plainly; though one of the Three Excellencies, he wore no finery and ate no second dish.

literal: A single bear-hide mudguard—decades without change; men of the time compared him to Yan Ying.
idiomatic: One bear-hide mud-guard he kept decades unchanged; his age compared him to Yan Ying.

literal: His residence was low and mean.
idiomatic: His house was humble.

literal: After he went out to command on the frontier, his sons and younger kin somewhat repaired it and raised halls and corridors.
idiomatic: After he marched out, his sons repaired it and raised halls and galleries.

literal: When Daosheng returned he sighed, "In the past Huo Qubing said that while the Xiongnu were not destroyed he would not build a home.
idiomatic: On his return Daosheng sighed: "Huo Qubing once said that while the Xiongnu were unbeaten he would not make a home.

literal: " Now strong foes still wander the northern wastes—how can I sit at ease in splendor!
idiomatic: Now fierce enemies still roam the northern desert—how can I dwell in comfort and splendor!

literal: " He sharply reproved his sons and ordered the house destroyed.
idiomatic: He sharply rebuked his sons and had the house torn down.

literal: In Taiwu's time wherever he served he won achievement; whenever he raised great counsel it mostly fit the moment.
idiomatic: Under Taiwu he distinguished himself wherever he served; his great counsels usually matched the time.

literal: As a general he had stratagem and kindly treated officers and men.
idiomatic: As a commander he was resourceful and kind to troops.

literal: The emperor ordered singing masters to praise the ministers in turn, saying, "Wise as Cui Hao, incorrupt as Daosheng.
idiomatic: The emperor had singers praise his ministers in turn: "Wise as Cui Hao, pure as Daosheng.
